newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Gesamtmetall gives up on sick pay cuts.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Gesamtmetall gives up on sick pay cuts.

text.p: Germany's Gesamtmetall employers group said on Sunday that a pay deal in the state of Lower Saxony, although unsatisfactory, would now set the tone for other wage talks in the metals and engineering sectors.

Gesamtmetall president Werner Stumpfe, speaking after a hurriedly-called board meeting meeting, told journalists that the agreement -- which guarantees full sick pay benefits -- had not met the federation's goal of cutting costs.
"But, realistic as we are, we see no chance for other regions to distance themselves significantly from this agreement," Stumpfe said.

Gesamtmetall had taken a hard line in failed national and regional pay talks on enforcing 20 percent sick pay cuts allowed by a new law. But the powerful IG Metall union replied with major protests to keep sick pay in line with full wages.
Stumpfe, the chief national Gesamtmetall negotiator, appeared eventually to lose the confidence of some local groups in a depressed industry which is losing 100,000 jobs a year.

First to give in to the calls to keep full sick pay were employers of 90,000 in Lower Saxony last Thursday. IG Metall also said on Sunday that some employers in the big southern state of Baden-Wuerttemberg had agreed a deal which mirrored the Lower Saxony deal "in all the main points".
IG Metall, which has close to three million members, has warned that all-out strikes are possible next year if deals are not concluded nationwide protecting full sick pay.
